problem: Object-centric scene graphs discard raw visual data, so a single detection failure is an irrecoverable memory omission; view-based snapshot memories are sparse and view-dependent, so a target seen from a bad angle cannot be re-examined. Both lack post-hoc re-observability.
motivation: Embodied agents must accumulate and reuse spatial knowledge over long horizons (EQA, lifelong navigation). Humans can mentally revisit a scene from a new perspective, whereas current agents are locked into their initial observations. A dense, re-renderable 3DGS memory could allow rendering optimal views of past regions without physically revisiting them.
key_idea: Use an online-built 3D Gaussian Splatting map with an optimization-free language field as persistent memory, retrieve regions via scene graph plus language field, render optimal novel views for VLM reasoning, and explore with a hybrid VLM-semantic and 3DGS-information-gain frontier score.
insight: The language field is the most critical component: removing CLIP drops SR from 71.1 to 66.6 on the GOAT-Bench 10% ablation, because it recovers targets the detector missed (case studies of the white robe, ficus tree and white door). Hybrid exploration mainly improves SPL (51.9 vs 47.8 without), while viewpoint selection and diffusion enhancement each add ~1-3 SR points. Gains over 3D-Mem are larger on lifelong GOAT-Bench (+4.3 SR) than on A-EQA (+2.8), consistent with the benefit of persistent memory over long horizons.
method: 3DGS mapping: RGB-D keyframes chosen by RAFT optical-flow threshold, sliding window of 10 plus 2 random keyframes, L1 RGB and depth losses, SH degree 0

Online language field: dense pixel-wise CLIP (SED + super-resolution decoder, compressed 768->32 dims) lifted to Gaussians by weight-consistent reverse aggregation using the alpha-blending weights, with no optimization

Parallel object-level scene graph (ConceptGraphs-style) plus TSDF and frontier maps; the VLM ranks objects (top-K_obj) for object ROIs, while CLIP text queries plus cosine threshold and KD-tree clustering give semantic ROIs (top-K_cluster)

Optimal viewpoint selection: 108 candidate poses per ROI (36 azimuths x 3 elevations), TSDF filtering, S_vis (14 points ray-marched) + Gaussian area score S_A to keep top-10, then 3DGS opacity score S_opa for the final choice
ROI rendering and reasoning: render the chosen viewpoint plus the best-detection pose, enhance with single-step diffusion (Difix3D+), and feed to the VLM to decide if the question is answerable

Hybrid frontier exploration: VLM semantic score s_sem used if max > tau_s; otherwise a geometric coverage score from the trace of the incremental Fisher information of the 3DGS (T-optimality surrogate for D-optimality information gain)

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, via API) as VLM; pretrained CLIP/SED, RAFT, Difix3D+ (frozen); Qwen3-VL-8B used only in runtime analysis
setting.training_data: none (training-free / zero-shot; the 3DGS map is built online per episode)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (three surrounding views per step) with poses
setting.action_space: frontier-based waypoint selection on occupancy/TSDF map (high-level goals)
setting.privileged: none stated (agent uses poses/depth from the simulator)

results: On A-EQA GSMem reaches LLM-Match 55.4 and SPL 43.8, beating 3D-Mem (52.6/42.0). On GOAT-Bench val-unseen it reaches SR 67.2 and SPL 46.9 versus 3D-Mem 62.9/44.7 and MTU3D 47.2/27.7. Runtime is about 1.2 s per step with an offline Qwen3-VL-8B and no diffusion.
limitations: Depends on the GPT-4o API and single-step diffusion for the best results, and the real-world runtime estimate drops diffusion; no actual real-robot experiments
Assumes accurate poses and RGB-D from the simulator; the 3DGS map is built online with limited fidelity for novel views
Ablations are only on a 10% GOAT-Bench subset and gains on A-EQA are modest
